text:
mike: FYI - starting ~15:04 UTC we saw a burst of nvme read latency in us-west1 that caused a few GPU attach timeouts. Attaches fall back forever until node reboots. looks tied to snapshot cleanup job that ran ~15:00.

sarah: any logs or controller output?

mike: pasting minimal iostat and dmesg snippet
```
# iostat -xz 1 3
avg-cpu:  %user   %nice %system %iowait  %steal   %idle
           2.14    0.00    1.22    86.41    0.00   10.23
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s r_await w_await aqu-sz  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.20    0.05     12     100     0.00    0.00  320.50  12.30   0.75  2.00  85.00
```
```
[  905.123456] nvme nvme0: I/O 12345 timeout, status: 110
[  905.123457] nvme nvme0: queue 0 timeout waiting for completions
```

kai: that r_await is wild. snapshot cleanup usually does heavy reads/writes but not 320ms r_await. what snapshot job? cloud-snap-cleaner? tag run id?

mike: yes cloud-snap-cleaner job id snap-2026-03-21-1500. It was doing concurrent snapshot consolidation on many nodes in the pool. I can repro on a spare node by running the consolidation with --concurrency=8.

priya: quick mitigation: can we pause consolidation for that pool and set janitor backoff? we should avoid node reboots (bad for customers attaching GPUs)

mike: paused job via ops UI. opsbot: Incident INC-4523 created for nvme read spikes in us-west1. dialed down concurrency to 2 on the running canaries.

opsbot: Reminder: run fstrim on affected nodes only after consolidation finishes. Do not run blanket fstrim while consolidation still in flight. :warning:

sarah: long term we should cap snapshot consolidator IO priority (ionice) and add a per-node concurrency governor. also consider moving consolidation to lower-prio windows per region.

kai: agree. also instrument kernel elevator usage. I saw the kernel changed io scheduler to mq-deadline in a recent kernel bump. mq-deadline sometimes starves NVMe under many small concurrent reads. try switching to none/blk-mq if safe.

priya: ops plan: 1) keep consolidation paused 2) throttle snapshoter with ionice and cgroups, 3) batch updates to kernel scheduler in canary, 4) add probe metric for r_await>50ms alerts. Who can own the probe? @sarah?

sarah: I can own the probe, will add a temporary dashboard and alert for r_await and nvme ops queue depth per host. Will also add a runbook step to check running snapshoter jobs.

mike: follow-up: for nodes that already hit the failure, a quick workaround that avoided reboot was to drain snaper processes, echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches then restart attach agent. still investigating root cause of nvme controller timeouts.

kai: pinging storage-firmware team to check for telemetry spikes: @storage-fw. there were similar controller timeouts in older firmware when heavy GC overlapped with host read bursts.

priya: cost note: if we throttle consolidation too low we'll extend snapshot window by ~3x which increases S3 egress and job runner time. need to balance iops protection vs snapshot latency. put this on next infra sync.

mike: thanks team — will keep INC-4523 updated with perf charts and remediation steps. :thumbsup:
